newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCL Energy set to outshine the FCL pack.
newsitem.headline: FCL Energy set to outshine the FCL pack.

text.p: Better-than-expected production from the Maui field plus an abnormal gain is expected to boost Fletcher Energy's net profit to around NZ$260 million when it reports on Wednesday.

The result, which will compare with NZ$57 million for the June 1996 year, was expected to justify the meteoric rise in FCL Energy's share price over the last two months and set FCL Energy apart from more modest outcomes for Fletcher Challenge Ltd's three other divisions.

FCL Energy's share price has been on a fast track since the company said on June 18 it would report net earnings of around NZ$250 million. The stock traded today at NZ$5.36, up more than a dollar since that forecast was issued.
The company will book an abnormal gain of NZ$32 million from the sale of its stake in Bay of Plenty Electricity to Power New Zealand .
Guy Hallwright at First NZ Capital said the result would reflect strong production and high prices in the first half. "It's been a great year for them," he said.
Hallwright added FCL Energy's share price had also been playing catch-up with some of its Australian peers.
One Sydney-based analyst said the Maui field, 68.75 percent controlled by FCL Energy, had exceeded expectations but the field would start to plateau in the current financial year.
He said FCL Energy's relatively short history as a separate entity from the FCL Group made reading the stock difficult.
Most analysts' models were still in their formulative stage, as evidenced by the recent under-recognition of the stock's likely earnings for the June year.
"I don't actually read too much into this result," the analyst said. "The trend is probably more important and the trend is downwards from this year onwards.
"Production, earnings, everything will start tipping over from now on, as I see it," he said. "As soon as that goes into decline it will start impacting immediately on production and profits."
Partly offsetting that would be growth from FCL Energy's Canadian operations and strength in onshore drilling, he said.
Fletcher Energy said earlier on Monday it expected a natural decline in oil production from its Maui field in early 1998.
